summary:
This bill appropriates funds for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for fiscal year ending September 30, 2025. It provides new budget authority across five titles, allocating specific dollar amounts to departmental components and activities, subject to numerous provisos, conditions precedent, transfer authorities, and policy riders that restrict the use of funds.

Title I funds Departmental Management, Intelligence, and Oversight. It appropriates amounts for the Office of the Secretary and Executive Management, the Management Directorate, Intelligence and Analysis, and the Office of Inspector General, each with specified period-of-availability extensions. Section 101 mandates a report from the Secretary to the Inspector General on non-competitive contracts, with a subsequent compliance review due February 15, 2026. Sections 105 and 106 impose new quarterly briefing and reporting requirements on the Under Secretary for Management regarding Level 1 and Level 2 acquisition programs and new pilot or demonstration projects exceeding $5,000,000 or 10 full-time equivalents.

Title II funds Security, Enforcement, and Investigations components. It appropriates sums for U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), including a specific $550,000,000 available until September 30, 2026, for operations and support. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) appropriations mandate not less than 50,000 detention beds and specific amounts for enforcement, the 287(g) program, and the Human Exploitation Rescue Operative Child-Rescue Corps. The Transportation Security Administration's appropriation from the general fund is subject to a dollar-for-dollar reduction based on offsetting fee collections. Coast Guard and U.S. Secret Service appropriations are also provided.

Administrative provisions in Title II include: Section 201 extends a prior pay cap on overtime; Section 207 prohibits new border crossing fees; Section 211 earmarks $600,000,000 within CBP procurement for steel bollard pedestrian barriers built to specified heights and containing anti-climb features, prioritizing locations from the 2020 Border Security Improvement Plan, with an obligation deadline of 120 days post-enactment; Section 212 prohibits dismantling existing border barriers except for simultaneous repair or replacement; and Section 213 prohibits funding for CBP One to facilitate parole. Numerous riders restrict funds for specific policies, including various immigration enforcement and prosecutorial discretion memoranda (Sec. 224), the use of a physical ID card for aliens (Sec. 230), and the reduction of 287(g) agreements (Sec. 218), while Sections 250 and 251 mandate no-cost-sharing contraceptive coverage for the Coast Guard under TRICARE, with effective dates 30 and 180 days after enactment.

Title III funds Protection, Preparedness, Response, and Recovery. It appropriates amounts for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), including a $22,741,000,000 disaster relief fund designated for major disasters as an emergency requirement. Federal assistance grants are allocated, including $520,000,000 for the State Homeland Security Grant Program and $305,000,000 for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program. Section 306 applies prior fiscal year reporting requirements on the Disaster Relief Fund to FY2025.

Title IV funds Research, Development, Training, and Services, including appropriations for U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), the Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers, the Science and Technology Directorate, and the Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Office. Section 405 prohibits funds for issuing employment authorization to aliens whose asylum application has been denied. Section 406 authorizes the Secretary to increase the H-2B visa cap under certain conditions.

Title V contains general provisions. Section 503 prescribes reprogramming and transfer notification procedures and thresholds. Section 505 allows up to 50 percent of unobligated FY2025 "Operations and Support" balances to remain available through September 30, 2026. The Act includes numerous policy riders that prohibit the use of funds for: implementing specified Executive Orders (e.g., 14008, 13985) (Sec. 546, 562); enforcing the "public charge" rule (Sec. 554); establishing a Disinformation Governance Board (Sec. 544); or carrying out certain climate change or environmental justice strategies (Sec. 560, 562). The Act rescinds $600,000,000 from prior CBP border barrier appropriations (Sec. 550) and $154,000,000 from the DHS Nonrecurring Expenses Fund (Sec. 551).
